transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-07-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 mins | Attendees: Lena, Marcus, Priya (Redwood) - Evan, Maya, Tom, Sasha (BrightForge)

Summary: quick renewal check-in to confirm capacity top-up, add UK VPC/private deployment option for data residency, align on benchmarks and procurement timeline. Some latency vs cost tradeoffs discussed; SE to run targeted tests.

Topics: renewal sizing, dedicated vs hosted, UK VPC onboarding, SOC 2/KMS questions, benchmarking plan, next steps/quote timeline.

Action items (read out): Lena to update quote; Marcus to run benchmarks; Tom to share network details; Maya to confirm success criteria; Sasha to confirm procurement window.

Transcript body: 
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everybody thanks for jumping on, hope that's — yeah okay, hi Evan, Maya, Tom, Sasha, nice to see you again. quick agenda, we want to confirm the top-up numbers you mentioned, talk UK VPC/onprem onboarding path, and next steps for procurement.
[00:18] Evan Park: yeah thanks lena, appreciate it. quick context - we've run steady for the past year on Redwood hosted, around 300M tokens/mo, but model usage has spiked. we need capacity for new customer-facing features and also need UK data residency for a small EU/UK subset.
[00:35] Maya Singh: and from ML, the models are stable but the latency tail has crept up during peak; we're evaluating whether dedicated capacity plus a regional node helps.
[00:48] Marcus Cole: totally, and that's what we wanted to show — dedicated pools let you pin capacity and route by region. quick caveat though, committed capacity changes throughput economics, so there is a cost/latency tradeoff.
[01:05] Tom Keller: one question — if we go private VPC in UK, what about egress and K-M-S integration? we need to ensure keys stay in our KMS and logs go to our SIEM.
[01:22] Priya Anand: that is doable; we have patterns for customer-managed KMS and we can stream audit logs to your SIEM, there may be minor differences in onboarding time.
[01:34] Sasha Lee: procurement — timeline wise we need a firm SOW by next week ideally, legal wants to know data residency and indemnities.
[01:46] Lena Ortiz: noted, we'll put that in the SOW. so proposed plan is: 2x capacity top-up on Dedicated, add UK VPC private deployment as a separate line item, 24-month term to lock pricing. does that align?
[02:02] Evan Park: sounds right but we need to see numbers first. also wanted to call out we talked to CloudAI and GigaServe — they quoted lower base price but their latency numbers looked worse at p95.
[02:18] Marcus Cole: yeah, benchmarking's key here. we'll run a 100-token chat and a 1k-token longer-run throughput test against a reserved pool that matches your expected concurrency, that'll show p50/p95 and sustained throughput.
[02:33] Maya Singh: would you also capture cold-start behavior and kv cache warming? sometimes our long chats rely heavily on KV cache reuse and if that's not warmed latency spikes.
[02:47] Marcus Cole: good call. we'll include prefix/KV cache warmup runs. apologies, sometimes the auto-transcript shows KV cash, but it's KV cache.
[02:59] Tom Keller: network details — we have egress via corporate proxy, NATed CIDR 10.2.0.0/16, and strict outbound port 443 only, with TLS inspection. can that be accommodated for VPC peering?
[03:16] Lena Ortiz: yes, we have a VPC-onboarding playbook; we might need a small customer NAT egress tunnel or private link. we'll surface options.
[03:28] Evan Park: security questions — SOC two status, iso 27001, where are logs retained, can we get a whitepaper?
[03:40] Priya Anand: Redwood has SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001 attestation; we'll send the reports and the log retention policy. for the private deployment, logs can be retained in your region and shipped to your SIEM.
[03:54] Maya Singh: and the KMS flow — do you support our HSM-backed keys? we need to ensure model inputs are encrypted and keys never leave our control.
[04:06] Marcus Cole: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported; in private deployments we integrate with your KMS and can support HSM-backed keys. auto-remark: sometimes transcript says KMS as K-M-S or K-M-ess.
[04:18] Sasha Lee: any SLA delta for private vs hosted? we care about availability during peak.
[04:26] Lena Ortiz: dedicated comes with an SLA for capacity and latency targets per the SOW. private deployments have operational SLAs but onboarding timelines are longer — we'll call that out.
[04:38] Evan Park: procurement wants staging timeline — how long to spin up UK private node?
[04:45] Marcus Cole: typical is 4–6 weeks from contract signature given network approvals; for rush we can compress to ~3 weeks with an add-on mobilization fee. but depends on firewall and KMS approvals.
[04:58] Tom Keller: okay 4–6 weeks is workable. can you show rough numbers for cost per million tokens and expected p95 latency for the UK node?
[05:10] Lena Ortiz: yes, the updated quote will have per-token tiers, committed rate card for Dedicated, and an add-on for private VPC in UK. expect per-token to be slightly higher for private due to infra and networking.
[05:24] Maya Singh: one more thing — we use a blend of model sizes; can Redwood route by policy so low-latency queries hit a smaller model in UK while heavy-generation tasks go to larger models in other regions?
[05:38] Marcus Cole: absolutely; Smart routing supports policy-based routing by latency and cost. we can set route rules and auto-fallback to a compatible variant if capacity is short.
[05:50] Evan Park: great. what's the handoff for benchmarks — Marcus to run tests but do you need sample prompts or will you use our perf harness?
[05:59] Maya Singh: we'll share a sanitized prompt set and a representative traffic trace.
[06:06] Marcus Cole: perfect, send the prompt set and a small traffic replay (anonymized). we'll run tests and share the spreadsheet with p50/p95/throughput and token costs.
[06:16] Sasha Lee: procurement note — we need the contract with regional addendum and data processing addendum (DPA) for UK. legal will want the DPA to be explicit.
[06:26] Priya Anand: we'll attach our standard DPA and can include region-specific clauses as needed.
[06:34] Lena Ortiz: okay last piece — success criteria from BrightForge on performance and cost. Maya, you want p95 under 180ms for the majority of chat flows?
[06:43] Maya Singh: that's our target for interactive flows, yes. for long generations p95 under 400ms is okay. cost per 1k tokens ideally within x% of current numbers; I'll put exact threshold in email.
[06:56] Evan Park: technical question — if we pin a ded pool in EU-WEST and UK node, will there be cross-region failover? we'd like automatic fallback but keep data residency concerns in mind.
[07:08] Marcus Cole: failover is policy-driven; you can choose to fail over for only non-sensitive traffic or to keep sensitive traffic local and degrade features. we can codify that in routing policy.
[07:21] Tom Keller: for the VPC peering, are you using direct connect equivalents or VPN? what are options for low-latency hops?
[07:30] Marcus Cole: options include private link, direct connect partners, or IPsec tunnels. we'll propose recommended network topology in the onboarding doc.
[07:40] Sasha Lee: procurement timing — if we sign by end of month, can you meet the August target?
[07:46] Lena Ortiz: yes, if sign by 7/30 we can aim for mobilization in the first week of August. otherwise it'll slide.
[07:54] Evan Park: ok that's helpful. any blocker on your side?
[07:58] Priya Anand: nothing immediate. just need the prompt set and the network details.
[08:04] Maya Singh: will you also provide cost simulation across usage tiers? helps us pick committed levels.
[08:11] Lena Ortiz: yes we'll include cost model scenarios in the quote.
[08:15] Marcus Cole: quick note — for benchmarking we might surface some model-quality delta when quantizing; we'll include quality checks against your eval prompts.
[08:26] Maya Singh: good. we don't want regressions just to save on token cost.
[08:32] Lena Ortiz: agreed — we'll include a small eval to compare.
[08:36] Sasha Lee: ok can we recap next steps?
[08:39] Lena Ortiz: recap: Lena send amended quote + SOW + DPA; Marcus run benchmarks with prompt set; Tom share network/CIDR and proxy details; Maya finalize success metrics and send prompt set; Sasha coordinate legal/procurement timelines. target dates as discussed.
[08:58] Evan Park: perfect. thanks everyone.
[09:01] Lena Ortiz: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and get those artifacts into the shared drive.
[09:05] END TRANSCRIPT
